seo.metaTitle: Grass Valley Workplace Injury Help | Free Attorney Consultation
seo.metaDescription: Hurt on the job in Grass Valley? Get a free consultation about work comp and third-party injury claims from an attorney who understands California law.

hero.subtitle: If a workplace accident sidelined you in Grass Valley, we can help you understand your options for both workers' comp and third-party injury claims at no cost. We'll work through the details without adding to your stress.

about.title: Grass Valley Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Grass Valley's economy runs on a mix of small businesses, contractors, warehouses, and service work scattered along corridors like SR-49 and S Auburn Street, and injuries on the job here happen in all kinds of settings — construction sites, retail stockrooms, delivery routes, and more. In California, workers' comp is generally the only path against your employer, but if a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker contributed to your accident, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside your comp benefits. That distinction matters, and it's easy to miss without guidance. We handle workplace injury claims and can look at what happened, explain your options, and help you understand deadlines that apply to any third-party claim. There's no cost to talk it through, and no obligation once you do.
commonInjuries: Falls from ladders, scaffolding, or loading docks

whyChoose.title: Why Grass Valley Workers Choose Us

items.title: We Help Sort Comp From Third-Party Claims
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually your only remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker may still owe you separately. We can help determine if that applies to your situation.

items.title: We Understand the Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and any third-party claim carries its own two-year deadline in California. Missing either window can limit your options, so timing matters.

items.title: We Know Retaliation Concerns Are Real
items.desc: California law prohibits employer retaliation for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you're worried about your job, we can explain your protections plainly.

items.question: I was hurt driving for work near SR-20 or S Auburn Street — does that change anything?
items.answer: It might. If another driver caused the crash while you were on the job, you could have both a workers' comp claim and a separate third-party injury claim against that driver. We can look at the specifics and explain how the two claims might work together.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting a workplace injury in Grass Valley?
items.answer: No — California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a workers' comp claim. If you're experiencing pushback, it's worth discussing with us sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if my injury happened because of faulty equipment, not my employer's actions?
items.answer: Workers' comp typically covers you regardless of fault, but if a third party like an equipment manufacturer or a subcontractor's negligence contributed to the accident, you may have an additional claim outside the comp system. That claim carries its own two-year deadline, so it's worth exploring promptly.
